topic: Finance Bill, Money Bill, Appropriation Bill — mixed tiers
description: Articles 110, 117, 112, 114, distinction money/finance bill, presidential roles, recent amendments

questions.stem: A 'Money Bill' is defined under which Article of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Money Bill — defined in Article 110(1). Must contain ONLY provisions dealing with: (a) imposition / abolition / remission / variation of tax; (b) regulation of borrowing by Government of India; (c) custody / withdrawal from Consolidated Fund or Contingency Fund; (d) appropriation from Consolidated Fund; (e) declaring expenditure as 'charged' on Consolidated Fund; (f) receipts on/issue from Consolidated Fund or audit of Centre/State; (g) any matter incidental to (a)-(f). The SPEAKER of Lok Sabha decides whether a bill is a Money Bill — and her decision is FINAL (not justiciable in earlier rulings; recent SC questioning in Aadhaar / RTI cases). Article 109 — procedure for Money Bills. Article 117 — Financial Bills.

questions.stem: Regarding the procedure for a Money Bill, which is INCORRECT?

options.option_text: It can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha (not Rajya Sabha)
It can be introduced only on the recommendation of the President
Rajya Sabha can amend / reject it like any other bill
Rajya Sabha must return the Money Bill within 14 days, with or without recommendations; Lok Sabha may accept or reject

questions.explanation: Money Bill procedure (Articles 109 + 110): (1) Introduced ONLY in Lok Sabha; (2) ONLY on Presidential recommendation; (3) Once passed by Lok Sabha, sent to Rajya Sabha; (4) Rajya Sabha can ONLY make recommendations (not amend or reject); must return within 14 DAYS; (5) Lok Sabha may ACCEPT or REJECT Rajya Sabha's recommendations — its decision is final; (6) If Rajya Sabha doesn't return within 14 days, the bill is deemed passed in the original form. (7) Goes to President — who can ASSENT or WITHHOLD assent (no return for reconsideration, unlike ordinary bills under Article 111). This power asymmetry between LS and RS is a deliberate constitutional design — Lok Sabha (directly elected) controls public finance.

questions.stem: The Annual Financial Statement (Union Budget) is presented to Parliament under which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 112 — 'Annual Financial Statement' (popularly the Union Budget). Statement of estimated receipts + expenditure of the Govt of India for the financial year. Two parts: (1) RECEIPTS — Tax revenue, non-tax revenue, capital receipts (loans, disinvestment, recoveries); (2) EXPENDITURE — Revenue expenditure (recurring) + Capital expenditure (asset-creating). Charged Expenditure (President's salary, judges' salaries, debt obligations) — non-votable. Voted Expenditure — needs Parliament's approval. Consolidated Fund of India (Art 266) — into which all Govt receipts go. Contingency Fund (Art 267) — at the disposal of the President for unforeseen expenses. Public Account (Art 266) — Provident Fund, small savings, judicial deposits. Union Budget is presented on FEBRUARY 1 (since FY 2017-18 — earlier was last working day of Feb).

questions.stem: What is the difference between a 'Finance Bill' and a 'Money Bill'?

options.option_text: Every Money Bill is a Finance Bill, but every Finance Bill is NOT a Money Bill (a Finance Bill may include matters beyond the Article 110 list)
A Finance Bill cannot deal with taxation
A Money Bill needs Rajya Sabha approval

questions.explanation: Categories of Financial Bills: (1) MONEY BILL (Art 110) — strictly dealing only with Art 110(1)(a-g) matters. (2) FINANCIAL BILL CATEGORY-I (Art 117(1)) — contains Art 110 matters PLUS other matters (e.g., bill that has tax clauses + general administration). Procedure as Money Bill for introduction (LS only, President recommendation), but Rajya Sabha can amend or reject like an ordinary bill. (3) FINANCIAL BILL CATEGORY-II (Art 117(3)) — does NOT contain Art 110 matters but involves expenditure from Consolidated Fund. Like an ordinary bill except needs President's recommendation for consideration (not for introduction). The annual Finance Bill that gives effect to budget proposals (taxes, etc.) is typically a FINANCIAL BILL CATEGORY-I or sometimes a MONEY BILL depending on its content. Speaker certifies which.

questions.stem: An 'Appropriation Bill' is required because, under the Constitution:

options.option_text: Money cannot be spent without the President's signature
No money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India except by appropriation made by law (Article 114)
It is required for income tax
Only Rajya Sabha can authorise spending

questions.explanation: Article 114 — Appropriation Bill. After Demands for Grants are voted on by Lok Sabha (within the Parliamentary Budget process), the Appropriation Bill is introduced — providing legal authority for withdrawal from Consolidated Fund. NO AMENDMENTS that vary the amount or change destination of grants are admissible. Once passed, becomes the Appropriation Act. The Finance Bill is separate — it gives effect to taxation proposals. Order of major budget steps: (1) Budget speech; (2) Discussion on the Budget; (3) Vote on Account (interim approval to allow government to function until full appropriation passes); (4) Demands for Grants; (5) APPROPRIATION BILL; (6) FINANCE BILL. CUT MOTIONS — Policy cut (token ₹1, expressing disapproval); Economy cut (specific reduction); Token cut (₹100 reduction, raising specific grievance).

questions.stem: Which of these CONSTITUTIONAL OFFICES has its salary CHARGED on the Consolidated Fund of India (i.e., not subject to a vote)?

options.option_text: Salaries of the President, Vice-President, Speaker, Judges of the Supreme Court / High Courts, CAG, etc.

questions.explanation: CHARGED Expenditure (non-votable; cannot be discussed in voting context but can be discussed): (1) Emoluments + allowances of the President; (2) Salaries + allowances of Chairman / Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha + Speaker / Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha; (3) Debt charges of GoI; (4) Salaries of SC + HC judges, CAG, UPSC chairman; (5) Pensions of judges; (6) any sum required to satisfy a court judgment. Reason for being 'charged': to insulate independent constitutional functionaries from political pressure (their salary cannot be reduced or held hostage by Parliament voting). VOTED Expenditure (rest, including ministers' salaries, defence, MGNREGA, etc.) — Lok Sabha votes on Demands for Grants, headed by ministry.

questions.stem: Who, as per the Constitution, decides whether a bill is a 'Money Bill' or not?
questions.explanation: Article 110(3) — 'If any question arises whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not, the decision of the Speaker of the House of the People [Lok Sabha] thereon shall be final.' SPEAKER's certificate accompanies the bill. Controversies — Aadhaar Act 2016 was passed as a Money Bill (despite covering broad provisions), bypassing Rajya Sabha. SC in K.S. Puttaswamy II (2018) upheld it but a dissent (Justice Chandrachud) called the certification a 'fraud on the Constitution'. Subsequent challenge — 7-judge bench in Rojer Mathew (2019) referred the question of whether Aadhaar was correctly classified as a Money Bill to a LARGER bench (still pending as of 2026). The decision is constitutionally final but increasingly seen as judicially reviewable on procedural grounds.
